title: Attention Trace Annotation and Sampling Protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a working protocol for instrumenting and sampling attention-heavy request traces so we can safely compare FlashAttention, paged-attention paths, and fused-op variants across mixed workloads. Focus is to get high-signal traces with minimal perturbation to scheduler and batching behavior.

Context / why this exists:
- We keep seeing non-deterministic tail latency spikes in production that correlate to certain kernel handshakes and queue-starvation windows.
- Existing traces (nsight, perfetto) give raw timelines but lack a shared naming convention to map kernel events back to conceptual stages (prefetch, handshake, compute, kv-copy, flush).
- Need a repeatable sampling and annotation approach for lab benchmarks and customer-facing bug reports.

Goals:
- Capture consistent event sets across FlashAttention vs paged vs fused ops with minimal overhead.
- Expose: kernel start/end, handshake/wakeup events, batch-coalescer decisions, KV cache hits/misses, and fallback path triggers.
- Provide a postprocessing script contract (jsonl output fields) used by dashboards and regressions test harness.

Quick rules (engineer-friendly):
1) Always collect two traces per experiment: cold-start (fresh model - clear caches) and warm steady-state (run 5k short requests to warm kv cache then sample).
2) Use 2 sampling modes: full-capture (developer desktop, nsight) and lightweight capture (production-like, CUPTI sampling + inline markers). Default for automated jobs: lightweight.
3) Keep trace window limited to 10-60s per run to avoid huge files; run repeated windows for statistical power.

Event naming convention (grep-friendly tokens):
- ATTN:KERNEL:FLASH:compute:start / :end  -- FlashAttention compute kernel
- ATTN:KERNEL:PAGED:tile:read:start / :end -- paged attention tile IO
- ATTN:PRE:KV:LOOKUP:hit / :miss -- KV cache outcome
- ATTN:COAL:DECISION:merge / :flush -- small-batch coalescer decisions
- ATTN:HANDSHAKE:GPU_WAKE / :GPU_SLEEP -- handshake and kernel handshake latency markers
- ATTN:FUSED:OP:<opname>:start / :end -- generic fused-op wrappers
- ATTN:FALLBACK:MODEL_VARIANT:<name> -- when routing falls back (e.g., int8->fp16)
- ATTN:TRACE:TAG:<run-id> -- unique run id injected at request start

Where to insert markers in runtime code (minimal instrumentation):
- Just before queueing a request: insert ATTN:TRACE:TAG with run id and request metadata (seq_len, prompt tokens).
- Before kernel launch: emit kernel-specific :start marker with batch_id and scheduler_elected flag.
- On kernel completion callback: emit :end with duration microsec and occupancy metric (if available).
- On scheduler/handoff: emit ATTN:COAL:DECISION and ATTN:HANDSHAKE events.
- On KV cache read: log hit/miss with prefix and shard id.

Sampling configuration recommendations:
- Lightweight (prod-like): CUPTI activity records + our tiny inline markers (writes to lightweight ring buffer). Sampling frequency: 1/50 requests randomized. Disable symbol resolution to save overhead.
- Full-capture (lab): Nsight Systems capture with GPU kernel names + CUPTI API callbacks. Use page-locked buffers for marker payload. Capture at 30s max.

Trace capture commands (examples):
- Nsight desktop quick (lab): 
  nsight-sys --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=attn_lab_{run}.qdrep --duration=30 -- ./benchmark --model foo --mode flash
- CUPTI lightweight (server job):
  LD_PRELOAD=/opt/tracing/libcupti_wrapper.so TRACING_MODE=light ./serve-bench --run-id={run} --trace-sampler=1:50

Postprocessing contract (jsonl lines, required fields):
- run_id (string)
- timestamp_iso (string)
- event (string, one of tokens above)
- seq_len (int as string)
- batch_id (string)
- kernel_name (string)
- duration_us (string)
- gpu_util_pct (string)
- extra_tags (comma-separated)

Example jsonl line (single-line string representation):
{"run_id":"r-20250301-13","timestamp_iso":"2025-03-01T13:02:15.123Z","event":"ATTN:KERNEL:FLASH:compute:start","seq_len":"1024","batch_id":"b-73","kernel_name":"flash_attn_forward_kernel_v2","duration_us":"","gpu_util_pct":"","extra_tags":"warm,slot12"}

Analysis heuristics (how we decide signal vs noise):
- Focus on event windows where ATTN:HANDSHAKE:GPU_WAKE -> ATTN:KERNEL:*:compute:start gap > 200us. Those are candidate scheduler-induced stalls.
- Correlate ATTN:COAL:DECISION:flush with increases in kernel launch rate variance; indicates coalescer thrash.
- For paged paths look at sequence of ATTN:KERNEL:PAGED:tile:read events followed by ATTN:KERNEL:PAGED:tile:compute - high IO latency spikes indicate page thrash.
- Tag runs by request entropy (many short requests vs few long sequences) and compare.

Debugging checklists (when you get a flaky tail spike):
- Is there an ATTN:FALLBACK event within 5s preceding spike? (model variant, quantization swap)
- Are KV cache miss rates high for that run_id?
- Do GPU occupancy metrics dip right before handshake events?
- Are there many ATTN:COAL:DECISION:merge events followed by immediate flushes? (indicates microburst)

Known caveats / instrumentation limitations:
- Inline markers add small overhead; keep payload under 64 bytes. Avoid heavy printf-style logs in hot paths.
- CUPTI sampling may miss very short-lived kernels (<50us) unless full-capture enabled.
- Nsight captures change scheduling slightly; use them for detailed root-cause but rely on lightweight traces for regression thresholds.

Artifacts to produce per experiment run (required):
1) jsonl trace (postprocessed) - compressed (.jsonl.gz)
2) summary CSV with aggregated quantiles for kernel durations and handshake gaps
3) a short notes doc (this naming) referencing the run ids and quick hypothesis
4) perfissues ticket if regression appears (attach traces and CSVs)

Short run plan (for next 3 days):
- Day 1: Add markers to fused-op wrapper and coalescer (PR in draft). Run warm vs cold traces for flash/paged.
  - linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/421
- Day 2: Run 50 stochastic windows with CUPTI lightweight sampler across mixed seq_len distribution. Produce aggregated CSVs.
- Day 3: If spikes repeat, capture 5 nsight traces for deepest analysis and schedule pair-debug with SRE.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add kernel GPU memory footprint to markers? (easy to get, might increase payload)
- How to standardize "request entropy" label automatically? (proposal: hash length distro per 1k requests)
- Get Priya to wire up run_id -> dashboard linking for quick drill-down.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and iterative. Look for missing event types that would help map scheduling decisions back to user-visible latency.
- If you add markers, add unit tests that ensure markers can be disabled at build-time.

Quick contact: Ethan Chen (slack: @ethan) — ping for pairing on PRs or trace uploads.
